struck: A 2026 annual membership is $2,685 for one person or $3,765 for two, plus a $25 cart fee a round.
use: Annual membership is $2,685 for one person, plus a $25 cart fee a round, or $3,765 for two, plus $25 a round each [club membership page, 2026].

struck: the lakes behind many of the houses, about 13 acres of water, belong to the neighborhood
use: the association owns three lake parcels of about 13 acres in all [Horry County parcel records]

struck: At the second gate, a guest can call the owner from the keypad, and the owner presses 9 on the phone to open it.
use: If the owner has filed the Gate Access Code form, a guest can pick the owner's name at the second gate's keypad and the owner presses 9 on the phone to open it; if not, the keypad calls the guard house [Dye Estates rules V3.0, 3.1.2].

struck: Owners use a key fob for its parking lot and for the beach gate.
use: The cabana has owner parking with key fob entry and key fob entry with private access to the beach [Barefoot HOA amenities page].

struck: In Dye Estates the ponds are only for looking at: no swimming, boating, fishing or docks.
use: Swimming, flotation devices, boating and fishing are banned on the Dye Estates lakes and retention ponds, and owners may not build piers or docks on them [Dye Estates rules V3.0, 7.1].

struck: The Grande Dunes Members Club course opened in 2005.
use: The course was constructed in 2005 [Members Club golf page].

pattern: dining room and patio look out on the 18th
struck: Its dining room and patio look out on the 18th green.
use: The club has indoor and outdoor dining seating with views of the 18th green [Members Club lifestyle page].

struck: The club says about 800 members belong.
use: The club's home page says '800 of your fellow neighbors' have made it their home away from home; it gives no member count.

struck: Grande Dunes Marina takes boats of 120 feet or more.
use: Grande Dunes Marina takes vessels up to 120 feet, and the marina says 'or more' [marina description on grandedunes.com and the master association page].

struck: The public two-mile Waterway Trail starts nearby.
use: The public two-mile Waterway Trail has its trailhead on Marina Parkway, near the Grissom Parkway overpass [grandedunes.com]. (Say nearby only after measuring the distance from the marina.)

struck: 137 Master in Equity deeds from 2010 through 2012, and 46 more in other years from 2008 to 2023 (183 in all).
use: The county recorded 182 Master in Equity deeds here from 2008 to 2023: 137 in 2010 to 2012 and 45 in other years [Register of Deeds index].

pattern: after 2008 many went through court-ordered sales\. That is why
struck: after 2008 many went through court-ordered sales. That is why builders are still finishing houses here
use: (cut 'That is why': no source ties court-ordered sales to the builders. Say each fact on its own.)

struck: the county measured The Bluffs as 370 feet from a proposed brewery site
use: A 2023 Post and Courier story puts The Bluffs 370 feet from a proposed brewery site across S.C. 31 [Post and Courier, June 2023].

struck: a Community Watch desk at its gatehouse on Bay Road, staffed 24 hours a day, seven days a week
use: The HOA lists Community Watch Desk coverage 24 hours a day, seven days a week, and a gatehouse phone line [HOA website].

pattern: \bits own maintenance staff\b|\bown maintenance staff on weekdays
struck: The association also has its own maintenance staff on weekdays.
use: The HOA lists maintenance coverage Monday through Friday, 7:00 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. [HOA website].

struck: The calendar adds bingo, yoga, Zumba, mahjong, card groups and a book club.
use: The HOA calendar has categories for aerobics, weekly bingo, yoga, Zumba, women's and men's cards, a book club, mahjong and crafts; the events are behind a login [HOA calendar].
